name: Central bank stress
summary: Bank of England widely expected to raise rates on 5 Nov; RBA hiked on 3 Nov
state: The Bank of England is widely expected to raise Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, as the energy shock lifts inflation (Yahoo Finance; HomeOwners Alliance). Australia's central bank raised its cash rate to 4.85% on 3 Nov. The Fed held at 3.75–4% on 28 Oct. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency move had been made as of 4 Nov.
for_you: Borrowers on variable or expiring fixed-rate loans are most exposed to rising rates; savers may see better returns. Lenders often reprice products after decisions.
rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma across major central banks = Watch

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — Bank of England expected to raise interest rates for first time since 2023

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
